headline: US stocks closed higher as softer June PPI eased inflation concerns and supported steady Fed policy expectations while megacap tech and financials led gains
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 (SPY) and Dow Jones Industrial Average (DIA) ended higher while the Nasdaq Composite (QQQ) closed lower, with Big Tech strength offsetting semiconductor weakness.
- The June PPI fell 0.3% in its largest monthly drop in over a year, with core readings below forecasts, reinforcing expectations that the Fed will keep policy steady.
- Consumer discretionary and communication services led the sector gains, with communication services up sharply on strength in Alphabet (GOOGL) and other large-cap tech names including Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), and Apple (AAPL).
- Financials climbed to record levels on strong bank earnings momentum, with BlackRock (BLK) jumping after robust results pushed assets under management above $15 trillion.
- Morgan Stanley (MS) gained after beating earnings expectations and raising guidance, helping underpin the broader bank rally.
- Semiconductor stocks declined in a rotation out of chips, with Micron (MU) falling sharply alongside weakness in SK Hynix (SKHY) and related names.
- PayPal (PYPL) posted a double-digit gain after reports of a roughly $53 billion takeover offer involving Stripe.
- Lucid Group (LCID) rallied with a steep double-digit advance on denial of bankruptcy rumors, while ASML (ASML) rose after announcing a large share repurchase and interim dividend.
- Pentair (PNR) dropped by double digits on softness in pool-related sales.
- After-hours trading saw no major earnings reactions above 2%, as investors turned attention to Thursday’s retail sales and labor data, upcoming results from UnitedHealth (UNH) and Netflix (NFLX), and geopolitical developments around oil and Iran.
